en: The Triplet on Destiny to Wrongness; The Triplet on the Wholesome.

Conditioned by a state that is neither fixed in wrongness nor unwholesome, a state that is fixed in rightness and wholesome arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition], there are six; ... up to ... under non-disappearance, there are six.

Conditioned by a state that is neither fixed in wrongness nor unwholesome, a state that is fixed in wrongness and unwholesome arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition], there are six; ... up to ... under non-disappearance, there are six.

Dependent on a state that is fixed in wrongness (*micchatta-niyata*) and is not indeterminate (*abyākata*), an indeterminate state that is not fixed arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] for the root; six for the predominance (*adhipati*) ... pe ... six for non-disappearance (*avigata*).
